"50X The Cash" has 119,634 prizes of $10 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $50,000 prize, with one left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Tomorrow's count on "50X The Cash" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
981.headline: The prize table, line by line

985.body:
The prize money on "MAX-A-MILLION" leans toward many smaller prizes. It is spread over thirteen prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $1 million. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

Every line of MAX-A-MILLION's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
985.headline: How prizes are split

988.body:
"Emerald 10's" is well into its run, with about a quarter of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Everything above about "Emerald 10's" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
988.headline: Early stage or late

990.body:
The most common win left on "LADY LUCK" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $1,000, and seven of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything here about "LADY LUCK" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through October 7.
990.headline: What's actually left to win

992.body:
The top prize count on "$2 MILLION VAULT" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has one of three top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

Everything above about "$2 MILLION VAULT" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
992.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

993.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "$5,000 Triple Play" are sold. The top prize count has held, with three of six still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

If "$5,000 Triple Play" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
993.headline: Four months, no top prize claimed

994.body:
The most common win left on "$25,000 Triple Play" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $3,000, and three of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

The table below shows the full count for "$25,000 Triple Play", with every prize level included.
994.headline: A close look at the prizes

995.body:
"$200,000 Triple Play" has two of four top prizes left and is in the second half of its run. About two-thirds of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Everything above about "$200,000 Triple Play" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
995.headline: How much has sold

996.body:
"$1,000,000 Triple Play" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. Of its unclaimed prize money, about three-quarters is in wins under $1,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

Tomorrow's count on "$1,000,000 Triple Play" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
